claims.statement: Datadog, LangSmith, Corridor, Notion, and Currents integrations issue hosted MCP or REST requests from the LangGraph server process with credentials on the provider connection, so their third-party keys are not placed in the task sandbox.

Team observability credentials (Datadog, LangSmith) are encrypted at rest with agent.encryption and stored in a dedicated team_credentials Store namespace kept separate from the plaintext team-settings record so a settings read never surfaces a secret.

load_datadog_tools builds a MultiServerMCPClient over streamable_http against Datadog's hosted MCP server, attaching DD_API_KEY/DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers, defaulting to the 'core' toolset and overridable via DATADOG_MCP_TOOLSETS.

The Datadog MCP URL is derived from the connected site by swapping its host for the 'mcp.' equivalent, and only a fixed allowlist of Datadog sites that expose a hosted MCP server is accepted when connecting.

The LangSmith tool surface is intentionally read-only: langsmith_get_trace fetches a single run (optionally with child runs) and langsmith_list_runs lists recent runs in a project capped at 50, calling the LangSmith API directly from the server process.
A LangSmith tool invocation resolves credentials per call, preferring the acting participant's own connected key and falling back to the team key only when allow_team is set.

Team observability tools are gated so prompt-injected runs from untrusted contributors cannot reach the team's Datadog/LangSmith data, because observability content (logs, traces, run inputs/outputs) is attacker-influenceable and can carry prompt injection.

is_observability_authorized authorizes a user who is a configured admin (CONFIGURED_ADMINS) or whose email is in OBSERVABILITY_AUTHORIZED_EMAILS, evaluated against the triggering user's config email, Slack email, GitHub login, and the email resolved for that login.

Observability tool grant is tiered: authorized users get Datadog plus LangSmith with team fallback; allowed-org members (ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS) get LangSmith with team fallback; everyone else gets LangSmith without the team key fallback.
The observability authorization check is left uncached because it reads per-run config, while the credential and org-membership lookups behind it are reused via TTL caches.

Corridor MCP config requires a bearer token from CORRIDOR_API_TOKEN or a token/api_key query parameter that is stripped from CORRIDOR_MCP_URL, and pins the URL to HTTPS host app.corridor.dev path /api/mcp, rejecting any other URL as unconfigured.
The Corridor integration exposes only the analyzePlan tool, filtering out every other tool the server advertises after the MCP handshake.

Corridor tools are registered as a lazy integration group so the MCP handshake is deferred until the agent requests the tool rather than running before every first model call, exploiting that Corridor's catalog is a static allowlist.

The system prompt instructs the agent to call Corridor's analyzePlan before substantial security-sensitive code changes and, if it is unavailable, to report that once and continue rather than retrying or treating it as a blocker.

Notion tools are backed by the hosted server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp using a per-user OAuth access token, and load_notion_tools uses a login only to read the tool list so tool schemas are identical for every user.

Each Notion tool is wrapped so its input schema gains a required on_behalf_of GitHub login, and at call time the wrapper resolves that participant, fetches a fresh access token for them, rebuilds the MCP tool, and invokes it — raising to reconnect if that participant has no Notion connection.

Currents tools are a read-only surface over the Currents REST API (https://api.currents.dev/v1) that lists projects, gets a run, finds a matching run, lists project runs, and gets a spec-execution instance, using per-user API keys encrypted at rest and sent as a bearer header from the server process.

resolve_participant enforces that on_behalf_of matches the user who triggered the run and is a verified thread participant, so the agent cannot use one person's connected credentials to act as another.

The Stagehand browser tools execute inside the thread's task sandbox, driving a sandbox-local Chromium including sandbox localhost via a long-lived runtime served over a Unix socket to which each base64-encoded request is dispatched.

Stagehand browser tools are enabled only when SANDBOX_TYPE is 'langsmith' and an API key is available for an anthropic or openai Stagehand model, defaulting to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 and overridable via STAGEHAND_MODEL.
Server-side integration loaders run behind a stale-while-revalidate TTL cache with a per-load timeout, and a timeout or exception yields an empty tool list rather than failing the run.
Credential reads on the tool-loading path are intentionally fail-soft: an unreachable Store returns no record so a run loses only its optional tools, while dashboard reads surface the failure.

Observability, Currents, Notion, browser, and Corridor tools are skipped for summary-stop and local/desktop runs, and the participant-scoped Currents/Notion groups load only when a triggering login is known.

LangSmith LLM Gateway routing is optional and centralised in make_model: a team setting overrides the deployment default, and supported provider calls are routed with a LangSmith gateway key while unsupported providers or missing gateway credentials fall back to direct provider calls.
Focused tests cover observability loader failures and wrappers, Corridor configuration and lazy registration, Currents contracts, Stagehand dispatch and enablement, and concurrent factory loading.
